text:
emma: Quick kickoff — I'd like to land a small 'Optimize heuristics playbook' doc + a curated sample corpus for validating batching/caching/quant profiles. Goal: one lightweight page in the docs + a /examples/sample-corpus.csv + a tiny benchmark script. Who can pick up the PR?

raj: I can start the sample corpus CSV. Do we have constraints on prompt length distribution?

emma: Good Q. Aim for a mix: 60% short (<64 tokens), 30% mid (64-512), 10% long (512-2048). Include a few multi-turn chat examples and embedding-sized short prompts.

liam: I'll draft the playbook text. Suggest sections: when to use KV prefetch, recommended batch sizes by model family, quant profile tradeoffs (int8 vs q2_k), and a short checklist for regression testing.

sofia: @liam can you include a tiny quickstart snippet for the SDK? People keep pasting broken examples. Example: `await client.generate({ model: "redwood-opt-3b-quant", input: prompt, batch_size: 8, kv_prefetch: true })` and a note about `stream: false` for microbenchmarks.

raj: Uploading initial CSV to gist: https://gist.github.com/raj/sample-corpus-1 (WIP). It has headers: id,role,content,expected_tokens. I added tags for 'embedding' and 'chat'.

emma: Nice — put a copy in the repo under docs/examples so the docs build can pull it. Path suggestion: `optimize/examples/sample-corpus.csv`. Also add a README that explains why each prompt was chosen.

liam: Draft snippet for quant profile section:

```
# recommended quant profile
quant_profile:
  dtype: qint8
  prefer_gpu_kernels: true
  fallback: float16
  safe_ops: [softmax]
```

liam: we should call out that q2_k can be great for latency but watch hallucination regressions on code and math tasks.

sofia: I'll add an SDK snippet for the batching helper:

```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()
for batch in client.batch(prompts, max_batch_size=16):
  resp = client.generate(model="redwood-opt-3b-quant", input=batch)
  # handle results
```

sofia: note in the doc that `max_batch_size` is a soft target; the runtime may split differently based on token length.

emma: For PR workflow: create a single PR that contains: docs/playbooks/optimize-heuristics.md, docs/examples/sample-corpus.csv, examples/mini-bench/bench.py, and updates to the SDK examples page. Tag reviewers: @liam, @sofia, @raj. Link the PR in this thread when opened.

raj: grabbing the PR number when I start. Also can someone add a tiny CI job to run the mini benchmark with `--smoke` so we catch obvious regressions in quant builds?

liam: I can add the smoke check as a GH action job (runs only on docs PRs) that runs bench.py with `--smoke` and verifies mean latency < threshold and no crash. Will add a note in the playbook about what the smoke checks assert.

sofia: small doc nit: we should avoid recommending absolute batch sizes (e.g. 32) — recommend ranges + a simple heuristic: `batch_size = clamp(ceil(128 / avg_token_len), 1, model_max_batch)` and show worked examples.

emma: Love that. Please include a table of example heuristics for 7B/3B/1B families. Keep the table tiny. Also add a short example of a failing case (long streaming chat) and what to change (lower batch_size, enable kv_prefetch, or route to dedicated).

docs-bot: New PR opened by raj: #6243 — "optkit: heuristics playbook + sample corpus + bench". CI: pending.

emma: Thanks — linking PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/6243. Assigning reviewers.

raj: Quick question on licensing for the sample prompts — should we add a license header? I'd prefer Apache-2.0 to be safe.

emma: Yes, Apache-2.0 in the CSV README and bench script. Add a short contributor note that prompts are synthetic or anonymized.

liam: Heads-up: when I run the bench locally with qint8 profile I saw a ~1.4x speedup for short prompts but a 5% output mismatch on the math test set. I added a note in the playbook draft: "Run evals/quality-checks on a small set of canonical prompts before rollouts."

sofia: We'll also add a link to the evals harness and a small example eval config (json) in examples/ so people can reproduce the quality check.

emma: Ok plan: land PR with docs + CSV + bench + smoke CI. Followup: create a short internal runbook for Dedicated customers about when to prefer dedicated routing vs quant fallback. Anyone want post-merge followups?

liam: I'll take the runbook.

raj: Updating gist -> pushing final CSV to branch now.

docs-bot: CI passed for docs linting. 1 failing smoke test (bench.py --smoke) on linux-quant-runner.

sofia: I'll triage the smoke failure. Likely the bench threshold too strict for q2_k. Will relax threshold or add platform-specific buckets.

emma: Thanks team. Once CI is green let's merge and then I'll pin the playbook in the Optimize toolkit landing page. :sparkles:

sofia: done — pushed a bench threshold tweak and small test harness fix. Re-running CI. :eyes:

docs-bot: All checks passed. PR #6243 merged by emma.

emma: Post-merge checklist: 1) Add link to playbook from /optimize routing guide, 2) Announce in #eng-ml, 3) Add a short note in release notes for this quarter. I'll take 1 and 3. Can someone post the announcement?

raj: I'll post a short announcement in #eng-ml after we verify sample-corpus metrics.

liam: Thx everyone. Small followup: we should run the benchmark monthly on the optkit examples corpus so we track drift after quant updates. I'll file a ticket.

emma: Awesome. Closing thread.
